Failover Recovers Quickly Again: The client now asks an edge whether it can actually carry a tunnel before moving to it, rather than only noticing afterwards that it could not. A recovered edge is used again within seconds instead of after a fixed five-minute wait, which previously made the client look stuck on a distant region long after the nearer one was healthy.

No More Phantom Region Switches: Each gateway is advertised under two names, and the client treated them as different places -- so a failover could 'move' between two names for the same server, logging what looked like a second outage while never going anywhere. One gateway is now one place, which also halves the health checks made when choosing a region.

Client Version In The Dashboard: The TUI header now shows which version you are running, and tells you when a newer one is available. That check also runs periodically rather than only at startup, so a client left running for days will notice a release instead of missing it entirely.

Accurate Node Reporting: The portal's tunnel list showed every session on the Control node, even when it was being served by a regional edge. Each gateway now records itself, so the Node column reflects reality.
Cleaner Restarts: Stopping the gateway normally no longer reports a failure, which previously made every routine restart look like a crash in the system logs and made real crashes harder to spot.

Failover That Recovers On Its Own: A brief edge outage now causes one clean switch instead of the client bouncing between regions. The client no longer returns to an edge that cannot actually carry your tunnel, edges report honestly whether they can reach the control plane, and if a session is lost the client re-registers within seconds rather than sitting with a dead tunnel until you restart it.

Fixed: Tunnels Left Serving Errors After A Region Switch. Cleaning up an abandoned session could remove the routing for the session that replaced it, leaving a connected tunnel whose public URL returned 502 indefinitely. This was the single biggest cause of a tunnel appearing to survive a failover while serving nothing.

Better Region Selection: If an edge is unavailable when you start the client -- during a scheduled shutdown, for instance -- that choice is no longer locked in for 24 hours. The client re-checks shortly afterwards and moves to the nearer edge once it returns, and the startup log now names any region that did not respond.

One Domain Per Tunnel: Starting a tunnel without naming a domain no longer registers it on every configured domain at once, which previously consumed several subdomain reservations for a single tunnel.

Tidier Multi-Port URLs: Additional ports now use a single dash, so a second port on 'alpha' is alpha-8081 rather than alpha--8081. If you expose more than one port, your public URLs change with this release -- update any bookmarks.

Security: Approving a registration now requires a deliberate confirmation rather than simply opening the link, so a link preview or crawler can no longer approve someone. The local Inspector rejects requests driven from other websites, closing a route by which a page you visited could change your tunnel's settings.

Reliable Edge Failover & Failback: Losing an edge no longer risks killing your tunnel. A transient gateway error during recovery is now retried against another region instead of exiting, a region you have failed away from is genuinely held out of the running until it settles, and a failback that doesn't work leaves you on the region you were already using rather than migrating you somewhere new.

Persistent Client Logs: The client now keeps a JSON Lines record of every proxied request and every diagnostic event under ~/.lfr-tunnel/logs/, for foreground and background runs alike. Region switches, lease evictions and exhausted failovers are all recorded, so a tunnel that misbehaved can be explained after the fact instead of guessed at. Logs rotate rather than overwrite, and request bodies stay off disk unless you pass -log-bodies.

Clearer TUI: The dashboard now shows the Inspector port it actually bound to and the target host you actually configured, rather than assuming 4040 and 127.0.0.1. Long paths and log lines are truncated by character, so accented text and emoji no longer render as broken glyphs.

Dependable Admin Email: Registration approval emails now reach administrators even if they have muted routine notifications, so unsubscribing can no longer silently block new users from being approved. Admin alerts also fall back to the configured owner when no dedicated notification address is set, and the gateway warns at startup if nobody would receive them.
Gateway Stability: Fixed several concurrency faults in the gateway and edge control channel, including a goroutine leak on every edge reconnect and races during startup and shutdown.
Self-Hosting Correctness: Self-hosted deployments no longer report tunnel status to this project's production gateway, and no longer fall back to its domain when promoting a reservation.
Dynamic TUI Scrolling Requests Table: Fixed TUI request history loop to display 8 newest requests at top, ensuring incoming HTTP requests update live.
Live Request Stream Rendering: Restores continuous real-time scrolling of captured HTTP requests in the CLI dashboard interface.
